children: RBI-approved Sunday opening gives customers an additional day for essential banking transactions before the proposed September 28-30 strike
Public sector banks and Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) are operating on Sunday, September 27, ahead of a proposed three-day bank strike scheduled from September 28 to September 30.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approved the opening of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on Sunday, giving customers an additional working day to complete transactions before the proposed strike.

Public sector bank customers can access branch services on September 27. Private sector banks are not participating in the proposed strike and are generally expected to follow their normal Sunday schedules, though customers have been advised to check with individual banks for branch-specific availability.
State Bank of India and Punjab National Bank have separately informed customers that their branches will remain open on Sunday to provide essential banking services.
Sunday Opening Ahead Of Three-Day Strike

The special Sunday opening is intended to limit disruption from consecutive non-working days. With Saturday being a holiday and the proposed strike covering Monday through Wednesday, banks could otherwise have remained inaccessible for branch-based transactions for five consecutive days.
The arrangement gives customers an opportunity to complete transactions requiring physical branch visits before the strike begins.
The decision to designate September 27 as a working day has, however, faced opposition from sections of bank employees.

The All India Bank Officers' Association (AIBOA), in a statement dated September 23, advised its members not to report for duty on Sunday, maintaining that the day is a holiday under the Industrial Disputes Act.

AIBOA has also said its members will participate in the proposed stay-out strike from September 28 to September 30. The association has linked the industrial action to its demand for five-day banking and other pending issues.
